name: dev.developmentradio/development-radio
title: Development Radio
description: Search podcast episodes on AI, security and software news; get sources and timed transcripts.

tools.name: search_episodes
tools.description: Keyword search over Development Radio episodes: titles, topics, chapter titles, takeaways, summaries, cited source titles and the full timed transcripts. Up to six keywords of three or more characters are used; a keyword matches at the start of a word. Episodes are ranked by how many keywords they contain, and when any episode contains more than half of them, episodes containing half or fewer are left out. Each result comes with its id, title, date, page URL, the best-matching passage (with a timestamp when it comes from the transcript) and the URLs of the primary sources the episode cites. Use this when you need a sourced account of a security incident, CVE, outage, AI or software-development news item, or an engineering practice such as lock expiry, replica lag, queue fairness or content security policy. The show's hosts are AI-generated voices.

query.description: Keywords, for example "nginx http2 rce" or "redis lock expiry".

lane.description: Only episodes in this lane of the show.

limit.description: Maximum number of episodes to return.

tools.name: list_episodes
tools.description: Lists Development Radio episodes, newest first, each with its id, title, date, length, lanes, page URL, one-line description and the URLs of the primary sources it cites. Use this when you need the most recent episodes, an overview of what the show has covered, or a valid episode id for get_episode or get_transcript. The show's hosts are AI-generated voices.

limit.description: Maximum number of episodes to return.

lane.description: Only episodes in this lane of the show.

tools.name: get_episode
tools.description: Returns one episode's show notes: summary, takeaways, the check the episode suggests running, chapters with timestamps, topics, every primary source it cites (title and URL), and links to the page, the MP3 and the YouTube video when there is one. Use this when you have an episode id and need its findings and sources without the full transcript. The show's hosts are AI-generated voices.

id.description: Episode id as returned by search_episodes or list_episodes, for example 2026-11-20-nginx-five-teams-daily.

tools.name: get_transcript
tools.description: Returns one episode's full timed transcript as Markdown, with speaker names and HH:MM:SS timestamps, preceded by its title, page URL and the primary sources it cites. Use this when you need exact wording, or to quote or locate a passage; get_episode is shorter when a summary is enough. The speakers, Maya and Alex, are AI-generated voices.

id.description: Episode id as returned by search_episodes or list_episodes, for example 2026-11-20-nginx-five-teams-daily.

tools.name: search_guides
tools.description: Keyword search over Development Radio's field guides: sourced, answer-first articles that each settle one engineering decision for Senior and Staff engineers, such as a caching pattern or a database schema change. Matches titles, topics, answers and the full text. Up to six keywords of three or more characters are used; a keyword matches at the start of a word. Each result comes with its slug, title, publication date, page URL, one-line description, topics and the best-matching passage. Use this when you need a reasoned engineering recommendation with worked numbers, real incidents from published postmortems and primary sources, then call get_guide with the slug for the full guide. Each guide is written with AI and checked against the primary sources it cites before publication.

query.description: Keywords, for example "cache stampede" or "schema migration lock".

limit.description: Maximum number of guides to return.

tools.name: get_guide
tools.description: Returns one Development Radio field guide as Markdown: title, publication date, page URL, the answer, the full text (the mechanism, worked numbers, how it fails in production, a decision table and a check to run), the primary sources it was checked against and the episodes that discuss it. Use this when you have a guide slug from search_guides and need the reasoning, numbers or sources behind the recommendation. Each guide is written with AI and checked against the primary sources it cites before publication.

slug.description: Guide slug as returned by search_guides, for example cache-stampedes-and-invalidation.
